officials.name: Christopher Konawel Jr.
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Commissioner Chris Konawel is serving his first term on the Gloucester County Board of Commissioners. He is an entrepreneur and small business owner, bringing his business acumen to promote economic growth. Chris lives in Glassboro and enjoys Jiu-Jitsu in his free time.

officials.name: Joann Gattinelli
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Joann Gattinelli is in her first term as a Gloucester County Commissioner. She was a small business owner for over 20 years and served as Mayor of Washington Township since 2017. A resident of Washington Township for 43 years, she was born in the Bronx, NY.

officials.name: Matthew Weng
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Matthew Weng is a Gloucester County Commissioner serving his first term. He has an extensive career in public service, including roles as a legislative aide, staff attorney, and in private practice. He also served on the Pitman Economic Development Committee, Pitman Senior Outreach Committee, and Pitman Borough Council.

officials.name: Nicholas DeSilvio
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Commissioner Nicholas DeSilvio is serving his first term on the Gloucester County Board of Commissioners, where he oversees the Department of Law and Justice. A Journeyman/Wireman for IBEW Local 351, he is also a Desert Storm Veteran who proudly served 9 years in the United States Navy as a Naval Nuclear Operator.

officials.name: Tom Bianco
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Tom Bianco is currently serving his first term as a Gloucester County Commissioner, overseeing the Department of Public Safety and Veterans Affairs. He has also served as Mayor of Clayton since 2012 and held leadership roles in the Gloucester County Department of Education & Economic Development and Workforce Investment Board.

officials.name: Jim Jefferson
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Commissioner Jim Jefferson is serving his fourth term on the Gloucester County Board of Commissioners and his first term as Deputy Director. With over a decade of experience working within government, Jim has previously served as a Constituent Relations Specialist and a Special Assistant to the New Jersey Speaker of the General Assembly. He was appointed to the NJ State Parole Board in 2010 and reappointed in 2016.

officials.name: Frank J. DiMarco
officials.address: 2 South Broad Street P.O. Box 337 Woodbury, NJ 08096
officials.bio: Director Frank J. DiMarco is presently serving his 8th term on the Gloucester County Board of Commissioners. He was chosen as Director on January 1, 2022, after serving three years as Deputy Director. A lifelong resident of Deptford Township, he resides there with his wife Marlene and their children.

officials.name: Jeff Kuhl
officials.office: Commissioner, Hunterdon County Board of Commissioners
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Jeff Kuhl is a sixth-generation Hunterdon County resident and COO at Kuhl Corporation with an engineering background. He has a long history of public service, starting on the Raritan Township Planning Board in the late 90s, and aims to support local businesses and preserve the county's rural quality of life.

officials.name: Shaun C. Van Doren
officials.office: Commissioner, Hunterdon County Board of Commissioners
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Mr. Van Doren was first elected to the Board of Chosen County Commissioners in 2018. He serves as a County Commissioner and holds various liaison and committee assignments, including Co-Liaison for the Budget Committee and Liaison for the Health and Human Services Departments. He has a background in project management and chemistry, and extensive experience in local government and community service.

officials.name: Susan Soloway
officials.office: Commissioner, Hunterdon County Board of Commissioners
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Susan J. Soloway is a County Commissioner for the Hunterdon County Board of County Commissioners, with her term expiring December 31, 2027. She has extensive government experience, including serving as a Franklin Township Committee Member and Mayor. Professionally, she is an accountant and holds a Bachelor of Science in Accounting from the University of Scranton.

officials.name: Mary H. Melfi
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Mary H. Melfi is in her fifth five-year term as County Clerk and has been a Hunterdon County resident for over 40 years. She served on the Flemington Borough Council from 1994-2006 and the Planning Board from 1993-2018. She is a Past President of the Constitutional Officers Association of New Jersey and the New Jersey Association of Counties.

officials.name: Renée M. Robeson
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Renée M. Robeson was sworn in as Hunterdon County Prosecutor on July 6, 2021, after serving as Acting Prosecutor since June 1, 2021. Prior to this role, she was an Assistant Prosecutor with the Mercer County Prosecutor's Office for over 17 years, where she led trial teams and specialized units. Prosecutor Robeson is a recipient of the Mercer County Victim Witness Advocacy Award and a graduate of West Virginia University and Widener University School of Law.

officials.name: Fredrick W. Brown
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Sheriff Frederick W. Brown is a lifelong resident of Hunterdon County. He served for seven years in the U.S. Naval Reserve and had a distinguished 31-year career with the Raritan Township Police Department, including seven years as Chief of Police. Elected Hunterdon County Sheriff in 2010, he aims to enhance public service and inter-agency cooperation.

officials.name: Heidi Rohrbach
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Surrogate Heidi Rohrbach was sworn into office on January 1, 2024.

officials.name: Zachary T. Rich
officials.office: Deputy Director, Hunterdon County Board of Commissioners
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: Zachary T. Rich began his public service volunteering on his hometown Finance Advisory Committee and Planning Board, and was first elected to the Board of County Commissioners in 2020. He works tirelessly for his constituents, driving results and ensuring fiscal responsibility. Zach enjoys supporting his wife Emily and daughters Juliet, Brielle, and Reagan with their passion for competitive cheerleading.

officials.name: John E. Lanza
officials.office: Director, Hunterdon County Board of Commissioners
officials.address: 71 Main Street, PO Box 2900 Flemington, NJ 08822
officials.bio: John E. Lanza has been a practicing attorney since 2001 and has worked with his family's Flemington-based law firm, Lanza and Lanza LLP, since its founding in 2005. He earned a political science degree from Boston College in 1998 and graduated cum laude from Seton Hall University School of Law in 2001. Mr. Lanza was first elected to the Board of County Commissioners in 2013 and is currently serving his fourth term.

officials.name: Rolando R. Lavarro Jr.
officials.address: 280 Grove Street Room 207 Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Rolando Lavarro became Jersey City’s first Asian and Filipino American council member when he was first elected in 2011, serving as City Council President from 2013 to 2019 and returning to the council in 2025. He advocates for affordability, transparency, and diversity, having championed earned sick days, living wages, and inclusionary zoning. A lifelong Jersey City resident, Lavarro has also fought to end ICE detention contracts and establish an Immigrant Affairs Commission.

officials.name: Mamta Singh
officials.address: 280 Grove Street Room 206 Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Mamta Singh is a mom of a teenage boy and a 6-year-old rescue dog, an immigrant, and also the executive director & founder of JCFamilies, the largest family community in Jersey City. She moved to Jersey City from India 18 years ago and has since been part of the local community, serving on the boards of several not-for-profit organizations and volunteering in local community initiatives. She started "Indian in Jersey City" in 2016 to support people moving from India to Jersey City. She loves dancing, biking, tennis, ping pong, badminton, and pickleball.

officials.name: Michael O. Griffin
officials.address:
280 Grove Street
Room 207
Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Born and raised in Jersey City. Michael Griffin has spent decades advocating for safer streets, vibrant shopping districts, expanded green spaces, and affordable housing in Jersey City. A staunch defender of residents’ rights, he partnered with local Leaders to pass the “Do Not Knock” ordinance, protecting homeowners from predatory solicitation. His work has consistently prioritized his community. As a former elected committee person under Mayor Glenn Cunningham, Michael developed leadership skills that continue to drive his community-focused initiatives. He has led economic development efforts, such as the Jackson Hill Main Street Special Improvement District, bringing resources and opportunities to underserved neighborhoods. As an advocate for affordable housing, Michael helped secure a 55% affordable housing project in his community. With a proven track record in advocacy and public service, Michael is ready to bring his vision of a stronger, more inclusive future to the City At-Large Council seat.

officials.name: Eleana Little
officials.address:
280 Grove Street
Room 207
Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Eleana Little is a neighbor with progressive values and a passion for public service. Prior to her election, Eleana was an active community advocate in downtown Jersey City, serving as President of the Harsimus Cove Association. Professionally, Eleana is an environmental engineer with degrees from Rutgers University and UC Berkeley and a decade of experience across both the public and private sectors. Originally from Central Jersey, she first moved to Jersey City 12 years ago, and currently lives in downtown Jersey City with her fiancé and their two dogs. She is honored to have the opportunity to serve the people of Jersey City on the City Council.

officials.name: Frank E. Gilmore
officials.address: 280 Grove Street Room 202 Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Councilman Frank E. Gilmore proudly represents Ward F on the Jersey City Municipal Council, serving with a deep commitment to equity, education, public safety, and community empowerment. A lifelong Jersey City resident and proud graduate of the city’s public schools, his leadership is shaped by lived experience and a clear understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing working families. He is widely recognized for his hands-on approach to constituent services and championing investments in historically overlooked neighborhoods.

officials.name: Jake Ephros
officials.address: 280 Grove Street Room 207 Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Jake Ephros is a teacher, tenant, former union organizer, and democratic socialist in Jersey City Heights. He worked as a labor organizer with 1199SEIU and helped lead Jersey City’s Right To Counsel campaign. He currently teaches Political Science part-time at Saint Peter’s University and is proud to represent Ward D on City Council.

officials.name: Joel A. Brooks
officials.address:
280 Grove Street
Room 207
Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Before being elected to the Ward B seat, Joel Brooks worked in the labor movement for twenty years, organizing with various unions. Born in Honduras, he attended New York University and now lives in Jersey City with his partner and daughter. He is committed to maintaining affordable housing for residents.

officials.name: Thomas Zuppa Jr.
officials.address: 280 Grove Street Room 207 Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Tom Zuppa is an attorney specializing in labor and employment law and civil litigation. He previously served as an Assistant Prosecutor at the Hudson County Prosecutor's Office. A graduate of Fordham University and Seton Hall University School of Law, he is focused on building a more affordable and equitable Jersey City.

officials.name: Denise Ridley
officials.address:
280 Grove Street
Room 202
Jersey City, NJ 07302
officials.bio: Council President Denise Ridley is a lifelong Jersey City resident. She earned her undergraduate degree at Hampton University in psychology with a minor in Spanish. Denise completed her master’s degree in industrial/organizational psychology at Montclair State University.

officials.bio: More information coming soon

officials.name: Anibal Ramos Jr.
officials.bio: Anibal Ramos Jr. serves as the North Ward Council Member for the City of Newark, bringing nearly two decades of dedicated public service, leadership, and community advocacy to the role. Since July 2006, he has championed initiatives promoting neighborhood revitalization, educational opportunity, and effective government. Ramos is recognized as an innovative leader focused on results-driven governance and equitable development.

officials.name: C. Lawrence Crump
officials.bio: Council Member C. Lawrence Crump is a lifelong public servant, legal professional, and civic leader dedicated to the progress of Newark and its residents. First sworn in as Council Member-At-Large in August 2021, he was elected to a full four-year term in May 2022 and began serving as Council President in September 2024. He proudly continues the legacy of his mother, former Council President Mildred C. Crump, and brings decades of experience in government, law, and community service to his role.

officials.name: Dupré L. Kelly
officials.bio: Councilman Dupré L. Kelly is a proud son of Newark, born and raised in the West Ward. A dedicated public servant, community advocate, and cultural ambassador, he brings a unique blend of grassroots leadership and global perspective to the Newark Municipal Council. Before entering public office, Kelly achieved international success in the music industry as a founding member of the multi-platinum hip-hop group Lords of the Underground.

officials.name: Louise Scott-Rountree
officials.bio: Rev. Louise Scott-Rountree is a lifelong Newark resident, minister, and Council Member at Large, bringing decades of experience in public service and clergy leadership. She made history as the first woman to serve as Manager of Clergy Affairs for the City of Newark and is a passionate advocate for faith, family, and community.

officials.name: Luis A. Quintana
officials.bio: Council President Luis A. Quintana is a trailblazing public servant with over 35 years of service to the City of Newark. Elected to the Municipal Council in 1994, he became the first Hispanic elected Council Member-At-Large and later the first Hispanic of Puerto Rican descent to serve as Council President and Mayor of Newark. Throughout his nine consecutive terms, Councilman Quintana has remained a steadfast advocate for the people of Newark, serving in numerous leadership roles.

officials.name: Michael J. Silva
officials.address: 920 Mayor Kenneth A. Gibson Blvd Newark, NJ 07102
officials.bio: Councilman Michael J. Silva, a lifelong Newark resident and son of Portuguese immigrants, brings over 25 years of law enforcement and community service to his role as East Ward Council Member. A graduate of St. Benedict's Prep and the Newark Police Academy, he served as a Community Service Detective. Deeply involved in the East Ward, he has worked with numerous civic, business, and cultural organizations, and actively supports causes like the American Cancer Society.

officials.name: Patrick O. Council
officials.bio: Councilman Patrick O. Council is a consistent and visible leader with over 20 years of administrative experience and community advocacy, serving as the South Ward Council Member. He is known for unifying and building collaborations, connecting residents and organizations to foster partnerships and expand access to essential resources. A lifelong advocate for youth and seniors, he is deeply committed to equity and progress in Newark's educational system and rebuilding a stronger South Ward.

officials.name: Ras J. Baraka
officials.address: City Hall 920 Mayor Kenneth A. Gibson Blvd Newark, NJ 07102
officials.bio: Ras J. Baraka is the 40th Mayor of the City of Newark, a native whose family has lived in the City for more than 80 years. Since taking office in 2014, Mayor Baraka's progressive approach has led to reduced crime, addressed affordability, lowered unemployment, and returned local control of schools. He is recognized nationally as a thought leader in urban revitalization and public safety.
